answer: A stake-weighted reputation ladder makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a deposit that grows as it climbs toward the summit of trusted counterparties, and every failed job slashes part of that stake. New accounts start at dawn with zero history, so they only get tiny tasks until a steady pulse of completed, verified work proves them. An attacker would need to fund and age thousands of deposits to fake volume, and one bad act wipes out the whole climb.
